prompt: In one sentence, distinguish prefill from decode in autoregressive inference.
reference_answer: Prefill processes the prompt in parallel, while decode generates subsequent tokens autoregressively.

prompt: In one sentence, explain why a KV cache reduces repeated attention computation during decoding.
reference_answer: A KV cache reuses previously computed attention keys and values instead of recomputing them for every decoded token.

prompt: Define time to first token in one sentence.
reference_answer: Time to first token is the delay from submitting a request until its first generated token is returned.

prompt: In one sentence, explain why tail latency matters even when average throughput improves.
reference_answer: Tail latency captures slow requests that may violate an online serving SLO despite higher average throughput.

prompt: State one condition under which prefix caching reduces prefill work.
reference_answer: Prefix caching reduces prefill work when requests reuse an identical tokenized prompt prefix.

prompt: In one sentence, explain why continuous batching can improve GPU utilization.
reference_answer: Continuous batching replaces finished requests with waiting requests so fewer decoding slots remain idle.

prompt: Name one reason a smaller model can have lower decoding latency.
reference_answer: A smaller model moves fewer weight bytes per decoded token.

prompt: In one sentence, explain why a serving benchmark records prompt and completion lengths.
reference_answer: Prompt and completion lengths affect prefill and decode cost and are required for comparable latency results.

prompt: In one sentence, explain what activation checkpointing trades for lower activation memory.
reference_answer: Activation checkpointing trades additional recomputation for lower stored activation memory.

prompt: In one sentence, explain why gradient accumulation changes optimizer-step frequency.
reference_answer: Gradient accumulation combines several microbatches before one optimizer step, reducing optimizer-step frequency.

prompt: State the purpose of loss scaling in mixed-precision training.
reference_answer: Loss scaling reduces gradient underflow when training with low-precision floating-point values.

prompt: In one sentence, explain why an evaluation split remains outside training.
reference_answer: Keeping evaluation data outside training prevents leakage and preserves an independent quality estimate.

prompt: State the role of optimizer state in AdamW.
reference_answer: AdamW stores first- and second-moment estimates used to scale parameter updates.

prompt: In one sentence, explain why gradient clipping can stabilize an update.
reference_answer: Gradient clipping limits excessively large gradients and helps prevent unstable parameter updates.

prompt: State one benefit and one risk of weight quantization.
reference_answer: Quantization reduces memory and compute cost but may introduce error that lowers model quality.

prompt: In one sentence, explain why deterministic seeds improve experiment comparability.
reference_answer: Deterministic seeds reduce uncontrolled run-to-run variation so experimental groups are easier to compare.

prompt: Under this experiment contract the teacher remains frozen. Explain why in one sentence.
reference_answer: A frozen teacher keeps the supervision source constant across student candidates.

prompt: State the purpose of an independent student baseline.
reference_answer: The independent student baseline measures how much quality the distillation treatment adds.

prompt: In one sentence, contrast fixed-trajectory and on-policy distillation.
reference_answer: Fixed-trajectory distillation reuses frozen responses, while on-policy distillation trains on responses sampled from the current student.

prompt: Explain why teacher and student use the same evaluation workload.
reference_answer: A shared evaluation workload makes teacher, baseline, and candidate quality directly comparable.

prompt: State what a model artifact content hash verifies.
reference_answer: A content hash verifies the exact bytes of the saved model weights.

prompt: Explain why a candidate must load successfully before delivery.
reference_answer: Successful loading proves the saved artifact can be restored for inference.

prompt: State why quality gain and teacher retention are separate gates.
reference_answer: Quality gain compares against the student baseline, while teacher retention measures the remaining fraction of teacher quality.

prompt: Explain why a tune decision must not create a deployable handoff.
reference_answer: A tune decision means at least one delivery gate failed, so the candidate is not deployment-ready.
